title: Cancellation Notice Required After a Patient Has Moved the Visit (In-Person Appointments)
content:
**4.1** Where the patient has moved an In-Person Appointments visit and the latest move was made **30 days or fewer** before the cancellation date, the notice days required for a patient cancellation of that visit rise by **2 days**.

**4.2** Where the patient has moved the visit and the latest move was made **more than 30 days** before the cancellation date, the notice days required rise by **1 day**.

**4.3** Where the patient never moved the visit, the notice days required do not rise.

**4.4** A visit has been moved by the patient when its appointment record shows one or more patient-requested reschedules; the reschedule count counts only moves the patient asked for, and the latest move is the date of the latest reschedule on the appointment record. The age of the latest move is the number of days from that date to the cancellation date.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Reschedule count | Latest move | Cancellation date | Days since the latest move | Rise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-10-14 | 2026-11-13 | 30 | 2 days |
| 1 | 2026-10-13 | 2026-11-13 | 31 | 1 day |
| 2 | 2026-11-10 | 2026-11-13 | 3 | 2 days |
| 0 | none | 2026-11-13 | not applicable | none |

### Notes

- The line sits at 30 days: a move exactly 30 days before the cancellation date falls in 4.1, and one made 31 days before falls in 4.2.
- A clinic-initiated move and the acceptance of a waitlist offer do not add to the reschedule count, so on their own they do not make a visit one the patient has moved.
